terms.meaning: the language that controls how things look, such as colors, sizes and positions
a drawing format made of shapes that the browser draws as pictures
an effect applied to a drawing, here used to make edges look hand-drawn
a list of steps describing how a style changes over time during an animation
a style rule that applies to the whole page, not just one component

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup
sections.what: Imports React so the file can produce the style pieces.
sections.why: Likely reason: required to write components in this file.

sections.name: DeskDefs
sections.title: Shared hand-drawn filters and patterns
sections.what: Creates an invisible drawing area with two wobbly edge filters, several fill patterns (checks, sparse dots, hatch lines, cork) and a small marker icon that other pieces can use by name.
sections.why: Lets pieces look hand-drawn and tactile without loading image files.
sections.watch_out: Other pieces refer to these by name, so renaming one here can make those pieces lose their look with no error shown.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 1)
sections.title: Colors, font and stage layout
sections.what: Sets the color palette variables, the retro font and size for the desk, the dark lights invert effect, and the fixed stage and frame containers that hold the desk.
sections.why: Keeps the color palette and font in one central place.
sections.watch_out: The font is named here but must also be loaded by the page, otherwise the browser falls back to a plain monospace font.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 2)
sections.title: Desk screen and title bar
sections.what: Sets the fixed 1200 by 800 pixel desk screen and the top title bar with its thick bottom border.
sections.why: Gives the desk a fixed paper size that looks the same on every screen.
sections.watch_out: Fixed pixel sizes do not resize by themselves, so a small window depends on separate scaling code that is not visible here.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 3)
sections.title: Stat pills and round buttons
sections.what: Styles small rounded labels with colored variants, and icon buttons that lift slightly on hover and press in on click.
sections.why: Gives the buttons a consistent tactile feel.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 4)
sections.title: Plant jars and corkboard notes
sections.what: Styles plant jars on the windowsill, which wobble when marked low, and sticky notes on the corkboard, with a hot variant.
sections.why: Decorative objects that make the desk feel like a real workspace.
sections.watch_out: The wobble only happens when some component adds the low class, and that component is not in this file.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 5)
sections.title: Corkboard pins and wall calendar
sections.what: Draws a pin on each sticky note and a lift effect on hover for the wall calendar.
sections.why: Visual detail for the corkboard and calendar.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 6)
sections.title: Paper pad and clock body
sections.what: Styles the lined spiral to-do pad and the blue clock body with its yellow LCD-style display.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 7)
sections.title: Bottom tray and its buttons
sections.what: Positions the bottom tray across the screen at a fixed height, and styles its buttons so the selected one turns dark with light text.
sections.why: Gives a navigation bar that matches the paper look.
sections.watch_out: The tray sits at a fixed height near the bottom, so anything placed in that lower band will be covered by it.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 8)
sections.title: Tray labels and room sheet
sections.what: Sets small bold uppercase captions for tray buttons, then styles the white room sheet with its border, header, and scrolling content area.
sections.why: Readable labels and the main content panel for each room.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 9)
sections.title: Knitted scarf strip and rivet buttons
sections.what: Styles the scarf strip used for habits, with a pop-in animation for each bar, and the rivet button style used across the desk.
sections.why: Makes the habit scarf feel like knitting and gives buttons a raised look.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 10)
sections.title: Coral buttons, dialogs and sleep animation
sections.what: Styles the coral variant of rivet buttons, the full-screen dialog backdrop and box, the dialog title bar, and a floating zzz animation.
sections.why: Dialogs need a clear overlay so they stand out from the desk.
sections.watch_out: The dialog backdrop uses a high stacking value of 100, so any other fixed piece with a higher value would cover dialogs.

sections.name: DeskStyles (part 11)
sections.title: Extra sleep and wiggle animations
sections.what: Adds a delayed version of the zzz animation and a small wiggle animation with a class name for it.
sections.why: Small playful motion for decorative elements.

summary: Holds the look of the desk: shared hand-drawn filters and patterns, plus all the CSS rules that make it look like paper, cork and a retro board.
purpose: Provide consistent styling so every desk piece looks like part of the same hand-drawn set.
why: Likely reason: keeping the styles next to the desk components keeps the look in one place. The reason is not stated in the code.
how: 1) The first component renders an invisible drawing area with filters, fill patterns and a small marker icon that other pieces can reference by name. 2) The second component renders a global style block with color variables, the desk font, the stage and frame, and rules for each object (jars, notes, calendar, pad, clock, tray, room sheet, scarf strip, buttons, dialogs) plus several animations.
inputs: None. Both parts are rendered with no props. Other desk pieces refer to the names defined here.
outputs: No visible content of its own. It defines styles and named patterns used across the desk.
risks: Global styles apply to the whole page, so class names such as desk-rivet could clash with other pages. Fixed sizes of 1200 by 800 pixels may not fit small screens. The font VT323 is named here, but loading it is not visible in this file.
debug: If something looks wrong, search this file for its class name and check its rules. If a hover or animation fails, check the matching keyframes. If dark lights looks off, check the rule that inverts the desk root. If a font is missing, check where the font is loaded, which is not in this file.
